0.comment: Lan Yan: Lan Junming, the Wind Reader
0.content: Lan Junming, called the Wind Reader, was one of the human Three Hermits of Guizang among the Eight Adepts who defeated the god Tao Dou. He first taught the Lan clan the Qimen arts. The Wuwang Kid nicknamed him "Mad Lan" (in return for being called "Red Runt") and later "Fool Lan". He was a carefree wanderer who studied whatever caught his interest, had no master, cared little for duty and invented his own arts. One of them was the Soul-Binding Art, which traps part of a soul in a rattan effigy and which the clan later forbade. In 7.1 a fragment of his soul, bound to a rattan puppet and sealed by his own hand, wandered Yilong Wharf at Moonchase saying "Moonchase ought not to be like this." Lan Yan saw through it, and with Zibai's help they identified him.

1.comment: Lan Yan: The Jade-Plumed Silverwing and the swallows
1.content: The Jade-Plumed Silverwing was a swallow adeptus and one of the Three Beasts of Tao Dou among the Eight Adepts. She was closely bound to the Wind Reader. Lan Yan's silver hair ornament is modelled on her, a Lan heirloom handed down so the clan never forgets its roots. Chenyu Vale treats swallows kindly, and the Lan family most of all: any swallow may nest under their eaves. Lan Yan has told the Traveler the old warnings. One says a swallow may take your place in death at the gates of Tao Dou; another, from her grandfather, says unkindness to swallows can bring an early death.

key: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon
2.comment: Lan Yan: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon (7.1 Moonchase event)
2.content: During the limited-time 7.1 Moonchase event, Chenyu Vale's associations, guided by the Lan elders, organised the festival at Yilong Wharf. It included a World Food Fair with cooks from Mondstadt, Fontaine (Escoffier) and Sumeru. Lan Yan wasn't picked to fight evil spirits with the Millelith and was happily acting as the Traveler's guide when she found the soul-bound Wind Reader. The search for "his" Moonchase led to Zibai and Zhongli, then to a Moon-Viewing Gathering at Wangshu Inn.

3.comment: Lan Yan: Springtime Charms and the border crisis (5.3)
3.content: During the limited-time 5.3 Lantern Rite, the Ministry of Civil Affairs invited Lan Yan to Liyue Harbor to help organise a street fair. Her grandfather's longevity readings had suddenly started telling everyone they had only a few years to live, and his only clue was "Wangsheng Funeral Parlor", so she sought out Hu Tao. Following her to Wuwang Hill, Lan Yan found Qiqi blocking a crevice, and both were pulled into the border between life and death. There they met Hu Tao burning fetor. Lan Yan kept them hidden with an illusion until the Traveler and Xiao got them out.

4.content: Lan Yan had heard of Director Hu but first met her face to face without realising it, while Hu Tao was out of uniform buying ritual perfume. Lan Yan was soon trapped with her in the border. She noticed that Hu Tao jokes about everything yet keeps her real plans to herself, and hopes her smiles will come from real happiness rather than from trying to reassure others. Hu Tao says Lan Yan is much stronger than she claims, and that her habit of curing fetor and illness is bad for the funeral business.

5.content: Gaming and Lan Yan have been friends since childhood. As a boy he trampled one of his family's baskets as a joke, and Lan Yan and her grandfather happened to visit that day to check the house's geomantic energies. She helped him repair it before he got into trouble. She remembers him as a "neighbourhood terror" who grew up, as she did. He still brings snacks wherever he goes and stocks up on hometown favourites before he leaves. He tells friends to let Lan Yan guide them to the best mountain food.

6.comment: Lan Yan: The Lan clan and Lan Yan's family
6.content: The Lan clan is an old thaumaturge family of Chenyu Vale who practise the Qimen arts taught by the Wind Reader, and they make rattan figures for exorcism. Lan Yan was born into a branch line. Her grandfather does geomantic house calls and tells fortunes in Yilong Wharf. Her parents are warm, practical people who give her silver for every milestone. In 5.3 she said her family were only distant relatives of the main line, and that she earns more from crafts than her grandfather does from fortunes.

7.comment: Lan Yan: Rattan weaving and rattan figures
7.content: Lan Yan is the Chenyu Vale Artisans Association's master rattan weaver. Chenyu Vale is famed for silversmithing, jade carving, dyeing and rattan weaving, and Mingxing Jewelry of Liyue Harbor sends buyers there. Her process: gather vines at dawn (stiff ones from old forests for screens, supple ones by the water for baskets), split the core from the skin, wash and dry them, then weave warp and weft with total focus. She makes furniture, screens, baskets, vases, hats, furniture covers and toys, and repairs heirlooms.
